name: relock
algorithm: rounds of one contested whole-file exclusive lock: a peer takes the lock on a handle of its own, holds it hold ms and releases it once (relock 0: the hand-off), or releases and retakes it at once every hold ms until stopped or 2 s pass (relock 1: the peer relocks); a waiter on a second handle of the same file calls the std's blocking lock, and a round counts when the waiter took the lock within 1 s. Prints the rounds and the rounds won, so a waiter that loses a round fails the checksum. Mk: File.Lock in a scope with a 1 s deadline, the peer a task; Rust: File::lock on a thread, the 1 s bound by recv_timeout, the peer a thread (README.md). MKH-47's relock measurement (status/rt8.md G-RT8-R4).

skip.c: not written: C has no std file lock (flock and LockFileEx are system calls, which the Rust and Mk cells reach through their std)
skip.zig: not written: Zig 0.17's std.fs.File.lock is a blocking call with no deadline and no second handle form tested here
skip.go: not written: Go's std has no public file lock (cmd/go/internal/lockedfile is internal)
skip.cs: not written: FileStream.Lock throws immediately on conflict and has no blocking lock

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the checksum counts the rounds the waiter won in time
notes: The hand-off time of a variant is its time per round less the hold: Mk's Lock waits on the kernel's hand-off on Windows (an overlapped LockFileEx on the poller, D-604) and polls with Io.Sleep from 1 ms doubling to 64 ms elsewhere, so on Linux a hand-off can take up to 64 ms after the release, and a peer that relocks every 5 ms can starve the waiter (the relock5 variant's checksum then fails).

The peer is a task (Mk) or thread (Rust) of the same process on a handle of its own, not a second process as status/rt8.md planned: both stds' locks are the handle's (LockFileEx) or the open file description's (flock), so the kernel sees two holders either way.
Written by evidence10 (M10, MKH-47's relock measurement, R10-67); its figures are development figures, labelled non-idle and provisional (R10-6).
